summary: Create unified onboarding gateway to provision Jira project, Confluence space, and ephemeral Slack channels with conditional archival
description:
Issue summary: Request a single self-service gateway that can create a Jira project, provision a Confluence space from a template, and create ephemeral Slack channels. Background: Platform and product pods often request identical sets of assets; ops spends significant time manually creating projects, setting permission schemes, and arranging compliance reviews for pods handling sensitive data. The goal is to automate provisioning with conditional approval gates (e.g., if a project is tagged 'sensitive' or 'external-collab' the flow requires compliance reviewer approval).

Request: 1) API/web form to request new project bundle (Jira + Confluence + Slack). 2) Approval policy engine that checks IDP group membership and triggers human review when required. 3) RBAC mapping so team leads get admin-level roles in the created spaces, while contributors get standard access. 4) Slack channel lifecycle rules: auto-archive after N days of inactivity, optional retention snapshot to Confluence before archive. 5) Audit trail: every provisioning event must be logged to a Confluence audit page and to an S3 bucket for long-term retention.

Acceptance criteria: The gateway must: - Provision a Jira project with company-standard permission scheme and issue templates. - Provision a Confluence space from the onboarding template and populate an onboarding checklist page. - Create Slack channels with naming convention, channel topic, and invite the initial members. - Enforce conditional approvals for 'sensitive' tags and log approval decisions. - Apply channel lifecycle policy (auto-archive + optional snapshot) and record the snapshot link in the space. - Emit an event to the ops audit bucket and create an entry on the Confluence audit page.

Risks/considerations: - Need to map IDP groups (Azure AD) to internal roles; changes must be reversible. - Slack rate limits on mass invites; consider staggered invites or service account. - Ensure templates do not accidentally expose private templates to external collaborators.

Timeline: Requesting a minimal MVP within 6 weeks: API + Jira/Confluence templating + Slack channel creation. Milestone 2 (12 weeks): Approval engine and archival snapshot automation.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint and web form that accepts project bundle requests
IDP group-based approval policy with 'sensitive' gating
Jira project provisioned with standard permission scheme and issue templates
Confluence space provisioned from onboarding template with checklist page
Slack channel created with naming convention and initial invites
Channel lifecycle: auto-archive after config threshold and snapshot link saved to Confluence
Provisioning events logged to Confluence audit page and S3 audit bucket
comments: Liam Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-14: Opening ticket — goal is reduce manual ops to onboard new cross-org initiative pods while ensuring compliance reviews for projects marked 'sensitive'.

Ava Patel (Assignee) 2026-03-14: Can you confirm which Azure AD groups map to the 'compliance-reviewer' role? Also propose using the existing service account 'svc-onboard-bot' for provisioning to keep auditability.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-14: Recommend implementing Slack invites via batched jobs to avoid hitting rate limits; for archival snapshot we can POST a Confluence export and store the zip in S3.
Maya Singh (Security) 2026-03-14: Need to ensure templates anonymize any PII before snapshot; include opt-in for customers with data residency requirements.
workaround: Manual provisioning using existing project-boot template and the onboarding checklist in Confluence. Ops must run invites and perform compliance review manually.
